clauses.text: 138 TWENTY-FOURTH BEPORT OF CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION. April 20, 1908. Mr. Alpheus H. Mahone may be reinstated as a fish culturist in the Bureau of Fisheries without reference to the time limit of eligibility prescribed by the civil-service rules. Mr. Mahone was appointed a fish culturist in the Bureau of Fisheries on August 6, 1902, and resigned on December 26, 1904, for the purpose of going to the Argentine Republic to assist that Government in establishing fish-cul- tural stations, having been suggested for this work by the Bureau of Fisheries* He was relieved from duty with the Argentine Republic on March 11, 1906, at his own request and in accordance with his contract The Commissioner of Fisheries stated that Mr. Mahone is a first-class fish culturist and recommended his appointment on account of the fact that it is very difficult to secure suffi- cient eligibles through examination. In view of these facts the Commission recommended the reinstatement of Mr. Mahone by Executive order. April 23, 1908. Mr. John Krey may be reinstated as an assistant engineer in the Engineer Department of the United States Army in the discretion of the Secretary of War and should the needs of the service so require, without reference to the time limit of the civil-service rules. Mr. Krey was employed from October 5, 1894, to August 2, 1901, with slight interruptions, resigning when his superior officer called another assistant engi- neer in consultation with respect to some work under the charge of Mr. Krey, who considered such action a reflection upon his ability and judgment and a breach of professional etiquette. Mr. Krey was reported to have been indus- trious and energetic and a practical and competent engineer, who accomplished results as long as he was in the Government service, and his experience has been wide and apparently successful since leaving it. The Chief of Engineers reported that there was no vacancy to which Mr. Krey could be assigned, but recommended some such action as would make his services available when a vacancy occurred, inasmuch as it would be an advantage to the service to gain a man who had been tested and found satisfactory. For these reasons the Com- mission submitted the above order to the President. May 1, 1908. The appointment of Mrs. Katherine J. Fen ton to a position as departmental clerk copyist draftsman, or copyist topographic draftsman, in the departments at Washington is hereby permitted without compliance with the civil-service rules. Mrs. Fenton is the widow of David H. Fenton, who was a member of the house of delegates of the general assembly of the State of Maryland in the year liXKS, and who died suddenly during the session of the general assembly. Mrs. Fenton was left a widow with two minor children who were dei>endent upon her. The general assembly of the State of Maryland urged the President to issue an Executive order in her behalf authorizing her appointment in the del >art mental service, basing the request upon the universal resi>oet entertained for the character of her deceased husband and the merits of Mrs. Feuton's case. While Mrs. Fenton had never passed a civil-service examination, she had served under temporary api>oiutmeuts in the Interior and Treasury Departments and in the Forest Service of the Department of Agriculture. The Interior De- IMirtment stated that Mrs. Fenton was a willing, faithful, and efficient copy- ist draftsman during the time she was employed in that Department. In the Forest Service she was employed as a copyist topographic draftsman and her work was found to be very satisfactory. In view of the circumstances the Com- mission saw no objection to the issuance of an Executive order in Mrs. Fen- i behalf.
